title: Integration
description: An integration writes entities into the catalog: its connector turns what a system has into items, each one object of one of its resources or its deletion, and mappings turn the items into entities of blueprints with jq.

metadata.description: What identifies the integration. Its icon and color come from its connector, so it takes neither.

mappings.description: One mapping for each kind of entity the integration writes from each resource. They're also the only blueprints it can write.

items.description: A gitlab mapping. Each item is GitLab's REST object as its lists give it, with what it belongs to under _gp: _gp.project, the project's full path, on everything in a project; _gp.group on members; and _gp.lastDeployment, the last successful deployment or null, on environments. A project carries what its default branch has, each null when it has none: _gp.defaultBranch, the branch, with protected and its commit; _gp.ciConfig, its CI lint, with valid, errors, warnings, includes and jobs without their scripts; and _gp.latestPipeline, its latest pipeline other than a child pipeline, as the pipelines resource gives one. A deleted tag or release carries only its name, or tag_name, and _gp, so identifiers must use only those. excludeArchived leaves archived projects out whole; a filter drops only the entities of its own mapping. The examples map each resource.

A sonarqube mapping. Each project is SonarQube's object as its project search gives it, with key, name and analysisDate, and under _gp: _gp.measures, its measures by metric key, numbers but for alert_status; _gp.qualityGate, its gate's status and conditions, or null if never analysed; and _gp.repository, the repository it's bound to, with alm and url, or null.

An authentik mapping. Each user is authentik's object as its user list gives it, with username, name, email, is_active, last_login, type and attributes, and under _gp: _gp.groups, the names of the groups it's in, counting those it's in through a child group as authentik does, and _gp.directGroups, those it was added to. Each group is authentik's object, with name and attributes, and under _gp: _gp.members and _gp.directMembers, its members' usernames the same two ways, and _gp.ancestors, the names of its parents, theirs, and so on. Attributes are whatever the instance's admins set, such as a mark that a group is a team.

type.description: portal: the portal's own users, groups, blueprints, integrations, actions and recent runs, synced one way. http: JSON fetched from URLs on a schedule, following pages, JSON other systems send to the ingest API, or both for the same resource. gitlab: GitLab's groups and projects and what's in them, read with an access token from GitLab.com or a self-managed instance, on a schedule and as webhook events. sonarqube: SonarQube's projects with their quality gate and measures, read with a user token on a schedule. authentik: authentik's users and groups with their attributes, read with an API token on a schedule.

config.description: The connector's config. The http, gitlab, sonarqube and authentik connectors take one; portal takes none.

env.description: An environment variable of the server, starting with GP_SECRET_.

secret.description: A secret, read from the server's environment, never written in the document.

authentikConfig.description: The authentik connector's config. Every sync is complete, reading every user and group the token's user can view.

url.description: The authentik instance's address, such as https://auth.example.com.

token.description: An API token, read from the server's environment, whose user can view users and groups, such as a service account with a role that grants both.

sonarqubeConfig.description: The sonarqube connector's config. Every sync is complete, reading each project with its quality gate, its measures and the repository it's bound to, under _gp.

url.description: The SonarQube instance's address, such as https://sonarqube.example.com.

token.description: A user token, read from the server's environment, whose user can browse the projects. Seeing which repository a project is bound to also takes administering it; without that, projects come without one.

projects.description: The project keys to read, each a key or a pattern with *, such as acme_*. Left out, every project the token can browse.

gitlabConfig.description: The gitlab connector's config. Every sync is complete. Once the server has GP_BASE_URL and GP_WEBHOOK_KEY, syncs set up a webhook on each project they read, and never remove one. Groups and members change only on a sync.

url.description: The GitLab instance's address, including any path, such as https://example.com/gitlab. Defaults to https://gitlab.com.

token.description: A personal, group or project access token, read from the server's environment, with the read_api scope, or api to set up webhooks too. Its user needs at least the Reporter role in each group and project read, and Maintainer to set up their webhooks.

groups.description: Groups read whole, by full path, with their subgroups and their projects. List a group or one above it, not both.

projects.description: Projects read on their own, by full path, such as acme/api.

historyDays.description: Days back a sync reads closed and merged merge requests, closed issues, pipelines with their jobs, and deployments. Older ones leave the catalog. Defaults to 30.

excludeArchived.description: Leave archived projects out, with everything in them. Defaults to false.

resources.description: The resources, keyed by the name mappings use. Each is fetched from a url, sent to the ingest API, or both.

httpPush.description: How requests to the ingest API are checked. Without a signature, pushes need an ingestion token.

signature.description: Lets a system push without an ingestion token by signing each request: an HMAC of the body, in hex, in a header. A signed push is always incremental.

header.description: The header the signature is in, such as X-Hub-Signature-256.

prefix.description: What comes before the hex, such as sha256=.

secret.description: The secret the system signs with, read from the server's environment.

httpResource.description: A resource. Its pull and push sides must give the same objects, since the same mappings run over both.

url.description: The http or https URL of the first page. {{ $since }} in it becomes when the last sync that fetched everything started, less a minute, on incremental syncs, and 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on complete ones. Left out, the resource is only pushed.

next.description: jq over a page, with the answer's headers as $headers by lowercase name, giving the next page's URL, absolute or relative to the page, or null on the last page. Left out, there's one page.

items.description: jq over a page giving its items, such as .deployments[]. Left out, the page is one item.

deleted.description: jq over each fetched item that's true when it's a deletion, for sources that list what was deleted.

maxPages.description: How many pages a sync fetches before failing, so pages that never end can't run on. Defaults to 100.

headers.description: Request headers, keyed by name. Write secrets as {env: GP_SECRET_...}, read from the server's environment, never inline.

httpReceive.description: The resource's push side: what a request to the ingest API carries of it. Its jq runs over the request as {body, headers, query}, with header names in lowercase.

items.description: jq giving the request's objects of this resource, such as .body.services[], or none.

deleted.description: jq that's true when the request's objects are deletions, such as .body.action == "deleted".

sync.description: Integrations that pull: how often to sync.

interval.description: A duration of at least 1m, such as 5m or 1h. Defaults to 15m. With complete, syncs at this interval are incremental.

complete.description: How often a sync is complete: a duration of at least the interval, such as 24h. A complete run deletes the entities that neither it nor the complete run before it saw, so one missed by chance stays. Left out, every sync is complete. The first sync, and the first after a publish, are complete too. Only http integrations whose urls use {{ $since }} fetch less on the others; portal and github ones read everything on every sync, and ignore complete.

mapping.description: Turns the items of one resource into entities of one blueprint. Every expression is jq over an item.

resource.description: The resource whose items it maps: one of the connector's resources, or for http, a key of config.resources.

blueprint.description: The blueprint whose entities it writes.

filter.description: jq over each item; keeps the items it's true for. Deleted items skip it.

entityMapping.description: Makes an entity from an item, with jq over the item. A deleted item only needs its identifier.

identifier.description: jq giving the entity's identifier, such as .id.

title.description: jq giving the entity's title. Defaults to its identifier.

properties.description: jq giving each property's value, keyed by the blueprint's stored property or relation. A relation takes the identifier, or a list of them, of the related entities.
